question.leadin: A meeting in this city was interrupted by Napoleon's escape from Elba.
question.text: Name this host of an 1815 meeting that established the balance of power of Europe in the 19th century, the capital of Austria.
question.clue: Antonio Salieri's opera The Stolen Bucket premiered in this city and Franz Schubert was born in this city known in ancient times as Vindobona.

swap.leadin: A bomb thrown at this leader's convertible bounced off and detonated under a nearby car.
swap.text: Name this Austrian archduke and heir to the throne of Austria-Hungary, whose assassination was one of the pivotal causes of World War I.
swap.answerHtml: Archduke Franz Ferdinand (or Franz Ferdinand Carl Ludwig Joseph Maria of Austria)
swap.clue: His wife was never permitted in the royal carriage, as a condition of his marriage to the lower-class woman after he became heir apparent following the death of his cousin Rudolf and father Charles Louis.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about scandals in the French Third Republic.
question.text: This Austrian reporter's experiences of anti-Semitism in the Dreyfus affair and elsewhere led him to plan the First Zionist Conference.
question.clue: He could not overcome the opposition of the Russian faction of his confederates to the Uganda plan, nor could he talk the Ottoman Sultan into giving him what he wanted.

swap.leadin: German Chancellor Otto Von Bismarck's statement that a "great European war" would start from "some... foolish thing in the Balkans" predicted the assassination of this person.
swap.text: Name this Austrian Archduke who was assassinated by Gavrilo Princip in 1914, kicking off a series of events leading to the start of World War I.
swap.answerHtml: Franz Ferdinand [or Archduke Franz Ferdinand Carl Ludwig Joseph Maria]
swap.clue: This Archduke of Austria, a nephew of Franz Joseph I.

question.leadin: The Pragmatic Sanction of 1713 was an edict issued by a monarch of this royal house.
question.text: Name this European royal house whose strategic marriages and inbreeding led to a namesake "jaw". Maria Theresa was the only female ruler of this House of Austria.
question.clue: Inbreeding devastated the genetics of this family, giving them a namesake "lip."

swap.leadin: One leader from this empire increased censorship by issuing the Carlsbad Decree.
swap.text: Name this empire home to a statesman who hosted the post-Napoleonic Congress of Vienna, Klemens von Metternich. This empire's combination with Hungary was dissolved after World War I.
swap.clue: This state deliberately provoked an 1846 serf rebellion in order to counter revolutionary szlachta.

question.text: As emperor, Napoleon married the Austrian princess Marie Louise, which was arranged by this Austrian foreign minister. This statesman helped established the Concert Europe at the Congress of Vienna, which he organized.
question.clue: The Academic Legion forced this man's resignation during the Revolutions of 1848.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Kingdom of Italy.
swap.text: The Kingdom of Italy fought against this nation and its ally Germany at the Battle of Caporetto which was a decisive victory for this nation. This nation used the acronym k.u.k to represent its dual monarchy.
swap.answerHtml: Austria-Hungary [or The Kingdoms and Lands Represented in the Imperial Council and the Lands of the Holy Hungarian Crown of St. Stephen; do not accept or prompt on “Austria” or “Hungary” or “Austrian Empire”]
swap.clue: This empire formed after the Ausgleich, which made Franz Joseph I its first emperor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about self-identified enlightened despots.
question.text: When asked his thoughts on the American Revolution, this Austrian ruler and enlightened despot replied, "Madam, it is my trade to be a King". This son of Maria Theresa liberalized the curriculum of the University of Vienna and abolished the Robot Patent.
question.clue: This ruler sent generals Lacy and Laudon on a series of tactical maneuvers in one conflict that saw little actual fighting, the War of Bavarian Succession, and, in response to the peasants' revolt of Horea, abolished serfdom.

swap.leadin: His service in the Wehrmacht in Yugoslavia and near concentration camps in Thessaloniki led to controversy during his 1985 presidential campaign.
swap.text: Name this controversial ninth President of Austria. He succeeded U Thant in an earlier post, but he was vetoed for reelection by the People's Republic of China.
swap.clue: His service in the Kozara mountains involved a massacre of Yugoslavs, and he was also a senior lieutenant during the deportation of forty thousand Jews from Salonika.

question.leadin: This ruler's foreign minister was Prince Felix of Schwarzenberg.
question.text: Name this ruler whose son Crown Prince Rudolf committed suicide in the Mayerling Incident. A member of the League of Three Emperors, this man named his nephew, the husband of Countess Sophie, as his heir.
question.answerHtml: Franz Joseph I of Austria [or Francis Joseph I]
question.clue: The Fundamental Articles of his minister of commerce and agriculture Albert Schaffle was denounced by German nationalists, and he appeared beside Alexander II in Berlin in 1873 in support of the Dreikaiserbund.

swap.text: Becoming the ruler of and following the Revolutions of 1848, he led his country into WWI before dying in 1916.
swap.answer: Franz-Josef I or Francis Joseph I

question.text: Before Balfour, Joseph Chamberlain worked with this man to establish a temporary Jewish homeland in the Uganda Scheme. This founder of Zionism discussed the "Jewish Question" in his 1895 pamphlet Der Judenstaat ("dare YOO-den-shtaht").
question.clue: With Max Norday, this man established the Basel Program, through which the Russian faction shot down the Uganda Plan put forward by this man.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about setbacks for the Austro-Hungarian royal family which presumably made Emperor Franz Joseph I a very sad man.
swap.text: In this 1889 incident, Franz Joseph's only son, Rudolf, murdered his mistress Mary Vetsera and then committed suicide, leaving Franz Joseph's brother Karl Ludwig as his heir.
swap.clue: Ida von Ferenczy was drafted to break the news of this event to Empress Elizabeth.

question.text: Your belief in Central Power unity was probably shattered following this affair late in the war. In this affair, Clemenceau published Emperor Charles I's correspondence with the namesake person asking for peace with the Allies.

swap.text: The "compromise" which formed the Austro-Hungarian empire is known in German by this name.
swap.clue: Friedrich Ferdinand von Beust ("boyst") supported this event in a failed attempt to exact his revenge over a defeat at Koniggratz.

question.leadin: Franziska Feifalik's elaborate hair care routine for this woman included a wash with egg yolk and cognac every two weeks to create her "crown braid."
question.text: Name this woman who commissioned a palace named after Achilles on Corfu as a summer refuge after a family tragedy. This woman was assassinated in Geneva by the anarchist Luigi Lucheni ("loo-KAY-nee").
question.answerHtml: Empress Elisabeth of Austria [accept Duchess Elisabeth Amalie Eugenie; accept Elisabeth of Bavaria; accept Sisi or Sissi]

swap.text: This statesman examined the herbalist Magda Logomer, whose 1757 acquittal ended Croatian witch trials. A report by this physician of Maria Theresa led to the prohibition of anti-vampire superstitious practices.

question.text: The War of Austrian Succession was fought over the right of this monarch to ascend to the Austrian throne, which went against Salic Law and was supported by the Pragmatic Sanction of 1713.

swap.text: For years, Haider was governor of this southern Austrian state, where he attracted controversy for his adversarial stance toward its native Slovene population.
